scriptFirstProductionGate20261112.priority: Spend more of the editorial effort on concept and manuscript BEFORE any AI Tuber generation. A script is not ready merely because it fits 35-40 seconds. It must be an educational, emotionally engaging, exciting mini-adventure with a visible payoff. This step is a hard pre-production gate, not a retroactive fix.
workflow: Write a one-sentence child-level learning objective and a separate one-sentence dramatic question the child wants answered; both must pay off on screen.
Draft 2-3 meaningfully different story paths (not cosmetic retellings). Choose the clearest with the strongest observable action, safe learning, and emotional payoff.
Write 3-5 truthful immediate visual openings; select an opening where Milo encounters a small tangible surprise/problem in the first 0-2 seconds.

Build a complete beginning / purposeful middle / solution / warm finale. Give Milo a real choice and attempt; make Miko and blue Pip active helpers. Avoid repetitive counting, generic lectures and arbitrary narration.

Use a scene-by-scene script + moving visuals + exact dialogue/voice + SFX/music + character/wardrobe notes. Every scene changes the situation or teaches something that leads directly to the ending. Let scene durations follow natural storytelling rather than rigid timed cuts.
Read the script aloud at a gentle preschool pace and test the logic from a 3-6-year-old viewer perspective: what is the problem, what happens, what do I learn, how do we know the solution worked?

Proofread numbers, colors, character identities and costumes against series bible. If any inconsistency exists, rewrite the SCRIPT before credits are used. Confirm no accidental dupes or preexisting jobs in AutoPilot.

Only after script-level approval consider new generation, with budget guard and prior no-paid-rework rule. Completed MP4 still requires complete audiovisual QC, correct Made for Kids and provider booking at 18:00 Europe/Oslo before release.

Is the story coherent, exciting, warm and age appropriate?
